dc31.title: Notifications dropdown
dc31.summary: A project-management app header. Make the bell show an unread badge and open a notifications dropdown, then mark items read.
dc31.brief:
The header of Tasklane, a project board. AppHeader renders NotificationsMenu (components/NotificationsMenu.tsx): a bell button that does nothing yet. The board below is static.

Read api.ts: getNotifications() (0.4–1s), markRead(id) and markAllRead() (0.3–0.7s each). components/NotificationItem.tsx already renders and styles one row (avatar, text, timeAgo, unread tint + dot): reuse it. utils/time.ts has timeAgo, isToday and a fixed NOW.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change (~20 min): Mark all as read.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–20 Core · 20–25 change · 25–30 Next, polish and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The badge needs the unread count before the menu is ever opened, so I load notifications on mount, not on open. I'll make one NotificationsMenu component that owns items, loading and open, and replaces BellButton. Unread count is derived with filter, never stored. Clicking an item updates it locally first and calls markRead in the background (optimistic). For click-outside I put a ref on the wrapper (bell + menu) and listen for mousedown on document only while open, removing the listener in the cleanup."
requirements: After getNotifications() resolves, the bell shows a red badge with the unread count (4), even before the menu is opened. The badge is not rendered when the count is 0
Clicking the bell toggles a 360px dropdown titled "Notifications" listing every notification with the existing NotificationItem. While still loading it says "Loading notifications…"
Clicking an unread notification marks it read immediately (dot and tint go, badge decrements) and calls markRead(id) in the background
Clicking anywhere outside the bell + dropdown closes it, and so does Escape. Clicking inside the dropdown does not close it
Group the list under two small uppercase headings, Today and Earlier (use isToday(createdAt)). A group with no items shows no heading

change.title: Mark all as read
change.html:
"Monday mornings people have 30 of these. Give them one button."

  • A Mark all as read link in the dropdown header marks every item read, removes the badge and calls markAllRead().
  • It is disabled when nothing is unread.

Hint: the same map + spread as marking one, without the if.

hints: State placement: NotificationsMenu owns items, loading and open. The badge and the list both read the same items.

Load on mount, not on open: the badge needs the count before the menu is ever opened. useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; getNotifications().then(...); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, []);
Derived: const unreadCount = items.filter((n) => { return !n.read; }).length; Then let badge = null; if (unreadCount > 0) { badge = <span className="bell-badge">{unreadCount}</span>; }
Positioning: search css position absolute relative parent. .notif-wrap { position: relative; }, then the badge and the menu are position: absolute inside it.
Marking one read without mutating: setItems((prev) => { return prev.map((n) => { if (n.id === id) { return { ...n, read: true }; } return n; }); }); then call markRead(id).
Click outside: search mdn Node.contains. Put a useRef on the wrapper that contains both the bell and the menu, and add a mousedown listener on document only while open (remove it in the cleanup).
rubric: Loaded on mount so the badge is right before opening
Unread count derived, not a second piece of state
Reused NotificationItem instead of re-building the row
Optimistic read update with map + spread (no mutation)
Mark all disabled when nothing is unread
Document listeners added only while open and removed in cleanup
Grouping done with derived arrays; empty group hidden

notes: min-w 18 · h 18 · pill · 11/700 · 2px white ring · top 3 right 2

primitives.name: Count matches: filter().length
primitives.note: Returns a number. Derive counts like this on every render instead of keeping a second piece of state that can drift.

primitives.name: Toggle with the updater form
primitives.note: The updater gets the latest value, so two quick clicks never read a stale open.

primitives.name: Update every item immutably: map + spread
primitives.example: [{ id: 'a', read: false }].map((n) => { return { ...n, read: true }; })   // [{ id: 'a', read: true }]
primitives.note: Returns a new array of new objects; the old state is untouched. Add an if (x.id === id) to change just one.

primitives.name: Badge / dropdown over a button
primitives.syntax:
.wrap { position: relative; }
.badge { position: absolute; top: 3px; right: 2px; }
primitives.note: absolute positions against the nearest ancestor that is not static. Forget position: relative on the wrapper and it flies to the page corner.

dc32.title: Onboarding wizard
dc32.summary: A fitness app sign-up. Turn the single Profile form into a 3-step wizard with validation, a step indicator and a final submit.
dc32.brief:
The sign-up screen of Stride. OnboardingWizard already holds the whole form in one form object and renders ProfileStep. The Continue button does nothing.

Read components/Steps.tsx: ProfileStep, PreferencesStep and ReviewStep are done (the first two take values, errors and onChange; ReviewStep takes values). Field already shows an error in red if you pass one. utils/validate.ts has isValidEmail and isIntInRange. createAccount(data) in api.ts takes 0.7–1.3s.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3. Change (~20 min): errors clear as you fix them.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–20 Core · 20–23 change · 23–30 Next (submit) and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The form object already lives in the wizard, so going Back keeps the values for free as long as I don't unmount the state. I add step (0, 1, 2) and errors. A pure validateStep(step, form) returns an errors object; Continue only advances when it's empty. The body is an if/else on step, and the title comes from a TITLES array. Later, submit sets submitting, calls createAccount, and when it resolves I store the account and render a success screen instead of the wizard."
requirements: Three steps: Profile → Preferences (PreferencesStep) → Review (ReviewStep). The eyebrow reads "Step 2 of 3" and the title changes per step. Continue moves forward, Back (hidden on step 1) moves back, and values typed earlier are still there

Continue validates the current step first. Profile: name required ("Enter your name"), valid email ("Enter a valid email"), age 13–99 ("Age must be between 13 and 99"). Preferences: a goal ("Pick a goal"). Errors show under the fields and the step does not change
On Review the button reads Create my plan: it calls createAccount(form), shows "Creating…" and is disabled while waiting, then shows "You're all set, {name}!" with the returned plan name
Review lists Goal by its label ("Build strength"), Workouts as "3 days a week" and Units as Metric/Imperial (check that ReviewStep gets the right values)

A step indicator above the eyebrow: three labelled steps, current one highlighted, completed ones show ✓. Completed steps are buttons that jump back to that step (values kept); the current and future steps are disabled

change.title: Errors clear as you fix them
change.html:
"Support says people think the form is broken: the red message stays after they've fixed the field."

  • Typing in (or picking) a field clears that field's error right away. Other errors stay until Continue.
  • Going Back clears the errors of the step you leave.

Hint: one more setErrors with the updater form inside handleChange.

hints: New state next to form: const [step, setStep] = useState(0); and const [errors, setErrors] = useState<StepErrors>({});
Write validation as a plain function outside the component: function validateStep(step: number, form: OnboardingData): StepErrors. It's easy to test and the component stays short.
"Is the errors object empty?" Search: mdn Object.keys. if (Object.keys(found).length > 0) { setErrors(found); return; }
Pick the body above the return: let body; if (step === 0) { body = <ProfileStep ... />; } else if (step === 1) { ... } else { body = <ReviewStep values={form} />; }
Change: clear one key with a computed property name: setErrors((prev) => { return { ...prev, [field]: undefined }; }); Search: mdn computed property names.
Stretch indicator: render each step as a <button disabled={i >= current}> and call onJump(i). Disabled buttons ignore clicks, so the guard is in the markup.
rubric: Single form object kept in the wizard (Back keeps values)
Validation is a pure function, run on Continue
Errors passed to the existing Field via the step components
Reused ReviewStep, isValidEmail / isIntInRange
Error cleared per field with a computed key (no mutation)
Submit shows a pending state and can't double-submit
Indicator derived from step; forward jumps impossible

notes: h 44 · pill · Back ghost, Continue filled

primitives.name: Is an object empty? Object.keys().length
primitives.note: Returns an array of the keys. {} is truthy, so if (errors) can't tell you it's empty; check the key count.

primitives.name: Partial<Record<K, V>>
primitives.example: const errors: StepErrors = { email: 'Enter a valid email' };   // other keys may be missing
primitives.note: Record<K, V> = an object with every key K; Partial makes each key optional. Good for "errors by field".

primitives.name: Computed property name
primitives.example:
const field = 'email';
({ ...{ name: 'x' }, [field]: undefined })   // { name: 'x', email: undefined }
primitives.note: The value of the variable becomes the key. Use it to update or clear one field without a switch per field.

primitives.name: Lookup by index
primitives.example: ['Tell us about you', 'What are you training for?', 'Check your details'][1]   // 'What are you training for?'
primitives.note: Arrays are 0-based: the 1st step is [0]. Show "Step " + (step + 1) to humans.

dc33.title: Poll with live results
dc33.summary: A gaming-community post with a poll. Vote optimistically and show result bars with percentages, then animate them.
dc33.brief:
A post in Guildhall, a dark-themed gaming community. PollWidget already loads the poll with getPoll() and renders the four options as buttons that do nothing.

Read api.ts: vote(optionId) takes 0.6–1.2s and returns the whole updated Poll (it moves your vote if you already voted). utils/poll.ts has percent and formatVotes.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change (~20 min): animate + "Saving your vote…".

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–20 Core · 20–24 change · 24–30 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"poll stays the single source of truth; myVote is in it. Results show when myVote !== null. On click I update poll locally first (+1 on the chosen option, set myVote) so the bars move instantly, then call vote and replace poll with the server's copy. Total and percentages are derived. I render the bar span in both states (width 0% before voting), so a CSS transition: width can animate it later."
requirements: Clicking an option votes for it immediately (optimistic): the options switch to results without waiting for the API, and vote(optionId) is called. When it resolves, the poll is replaced with the server's data
Results: each option shows a filled bar behind the label whose width is its percentage, and the percentage on the right ("10%"). Under the list: "101 votes · Closes in 2 days"
After voting, the options are disabled: you cannot vote twice
Your option has a ✓ next to the label and a stronger gradient bar

Change vote link in the meta line (disabled while saving): hides the results and makes the options clickable again ("Pick a new option" + Cancel). Picking a different option moves the vote optimistically (−1 old, +1 new; total stays 101) and calls vote; picking the same option just returns to the results

change.title: Make it feel alive
change.html:
"The results just snap in. Design wants motion, and people double-check whether the vote went through."

  • Bars animate from 0 to their width over about 0.6s.
  • While the vote is saving, the meta line says "Saving your vote…" instead of "Closes in 2 days", and the options stay disabled.

Hint: a transition only runs if the same element changes width.

hints: Derived: const total = poll.options.reduce((sum, o) => { return sum + o.votes; }, 0); and const showResults = poll.myVote !== null;
Optimistic update without mutation: setPoll((prev) => { ... return { ...prev, myVote: optionId, options: prev.options.map((o) => { ... return { ...o, votes }; }) }; });
Bar width: an inline style object, style={{ width: pct + '%' }}, on a span that is position: absolute behind the label.
Can't vote twice: disabled={showResults} on the option button.

Change: search mdn css transition width. Render the bar span in both states (width 0% before voting) and add transition: width 0.6s. A saving boolean set before vote() and cleared in .then drives the text.
Stretch: one boolean changing. showResults = poll.myVote !== null && !changing. In the optimistic update also subtract 1 from prev.myVote's option.
rubric: UI updates before the API resolves (optimistic)
Server response replaces the local guess
Total and percentages derived; percent() reused
No double voting (disabled while showing results / saving)
Bars animate via a persistent element + CSS transition
Saving state shown without blocking the optimistic UI
Change vote moves the count, total unchanged

primitives.name: Sum with reduce
primitives.example: [{ votes: 42 }, { votes: 9 }].reduce((sum, o) => { return sum + o.votes; }, 0)   // 51
primitives.note: Returns the accumulated value. Always pass the start value (0), or an empty array throws.

primitives.name: Inline style object
primitives.note: Double braces: outer = JSX expression, inner = a JS object. Keys are camelCase (backgroundColor); numbers mean px.

primitives.name: Animate a width change
primitives.note: Only animates when the same element changes its width. If the element is newly mounted, there is nothing to animate from.

primitives.name: Fire, then reconcile
primitives.note: Update the UI first (your guess), then replace it with what the server returns, since others may have voted meanwhile.

dc34.title: Inline rename
dc34.summary: A deploy dashboard's project list. Double-click a name to edit it in place, Enter saves through the API, Escape cancels.
dc34.brief:
The Projects page of Deployd, a hosting dashboard. ProjectList loads projects with getProjects() and renders a ProjectRow each. Each row has an Edit button that does nothing.

Read api.ts: renameProject(id, name) takes 0.5–1s, returns the updated project, and throws if another project already has that name. Read components/NameInput.tsx: a styled inline input that focuses itself and selects its text when it mounts, and shows an error if you pass one. StatusDot and formatAgo already exist.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4–5. Change (~20 min): show API errors.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–5 plan out loud · 5–20 Core · 20–24 change · 24–30 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Editing needs a draft separate from the saved name so Escape can throw it away. Only one row should be open, so the list keeps editingId and each row gets isEditing; the row keeps its own draft. Edit copies the name into the draft. Enter/Escape are an onKeyDown passed to NameInput. Save trims, calls the API, and hands the updated project up so the list can map it in and clear editingId."
requirements: Double-clicking a project name, or clicking Edit, replaces the name with NameInput holding the current name. The actions become Cancel and Save
Enter (or Save) calls renameProject(id, name.trim()). On success the row shows the new name and leaves edit mode
Escape (or Cancel) leaves edit mode and the old name is shown, with no API call
While saving, the input and buttons are disabled and Save reads "Saving…". The row being edited has a light tint
An empty (or whitespace-only) name is not saved: NameInput shows "Name can't be empty" and you stay in edit mode; typing clears it. Saving an unchanged name just closes the editor
Only one row can be in edit mode (opening another discards the first draft), and while a save is in progress the other rows' Edit buttons are disabled

change.title: Show API errors
change.html:
"QA renamed Docs to 'marketing site' and the row just… stayed there, spinning back to Save. No message."

  • If renameProject rejects, stay in edit mode, re-enable the input and show the API's error message under it (e.g. A project named "Marketing site" already exists).
  • Starting a new edit clears an old error.

Hint: .catch((err: Error) => { ... err.message ... }) and NameInput's error prop.

hints: Keep a draft string separate from project.name. Copy the name into it when editing starts; Escape just leaves edit mode.
One open row: const [editingId, setEditingId] = useState<string | null>(null); in the list, and isEditing={p.id === editingId} on each row. One id can only match one row.
Keys: function handleKeyDown(e: React.KeyboardEvent<HTMLInputElement>) { if (e.key === "Enter") { handleSave(); } if (e.key === "Escape") { onStopEdit(); } }. Search: mdn KeyboardEvent key.
Replace the saved project in the list: setProjects((prev) => { return prev.map((p) => { if (p.id === updated.id) { return updated; } return p; }); });
Change: renameProject(id, name).then(...).catch((err: Error) => { setSaving(false); setError(err.message); }); Search: mdn promise catch.
rubric: Draft separate from saved value; Escape discards it
Enter/Escape handled on the input
Reused NameInput (focus/select and error display come for free)
List updated immutably with the server's project
API error caught and shown; stays in edit mode
Saving state disables input and buttons
Single editingId in the list enforces one editor

notes: h 32 · max-w 320 · radius 6 · 600 weight · focus ring 3px rgba(0,112,243,.15)

primitives.name: Enter / Escape on an input
primitives.note: e.key is a string like "Enter", "Escape", "ArrowDown". Use onKeyDown, not the deprecated onKeyPress.

primitives.name: Replace one item by id
primitives.syntax: prev.map((x) => { if (x.id === updated.id) { return updated; } return x; })
primitives.example: [{ id: 'a', name: 'Docs' }].map((p) => { if (p.id === 'a') { return { id: 'a', name: 'Docs v2' }; } return p; })   // [{ id: 'a', name: 'Docs v2' }]
primitives.note: Returns a new array the same length; only the matching item is swapped.
primitives.search: react update item in array state

primitives.name: Handle a rejected promise
primitives.example: renameProject('prj_2', 'marketing site').catch((err: Error) => { setError(err.message); });   // 'A project named "Marketing site" already exists'
primitives.note: When the async function throws, .then is skipped and .catch gets the Error. Reset any "saving" flag in both branches.

dc35.title: School month calendar
dc35.summary: A school family portal. Replace the agenda list with a 7-column month grid with events, prev/next month, and a day panel.
dc35.brief:
The family portal of Maple Grove Elementary. SchoolCalendar gets a fixed today prop (Sept 15, 2026; never use Date.now) and shows this month's events from getEvents(year, month) as a flat list. The ‹ › buttons do nothing.

Read utils/date.ts: daysInMonth, firstWeekday, toKey, formatLongDate, WEEKDAYS, MONTH_NAMES. Months are 0-based like Date. EventChip renders one event. getEvents takes 0.4–0.9s.

Pass bar: Core 1–3 working. Strong: plus 4. Change (~20 min): cap the chips.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–20 Core · 20–24 change · 24–30 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The visible month is state, { year, month }, starting from today. The effect refetches when it changes; the starter's cancelled guard already stops a slow response for the old month from landing. The cells are derived: N blanks for the first weekday, then days 1..N, then blanks to fill the last row. Events are matched to cells by toKey. Prev/next use new Date(year, month ± 1, 1) so December → January rolls the year for me."
requirements: The agenda list is replaced by a 7-column grid with Sun–Sat headings (the Legend stays under it). September 2026 starts on a Tuesday, so the 1st is in the third column; blank cells fill before the 1st and after the last day so every row has 7
Each day cell shows the day number and an EventChip for every event on that date. Today (the today prop) has a yellow circle on its number
‹ and › change the month (title "October 2026") and fetch that month's events. Going back from January goes to December of the previous year
While a month is loading, show a small "Loading…" next to the title. A slow response for a month you already left must not overwrite the current one

Clicking a day selects it (green outline) and opens a panel to the right titled with formatLongDate ("Tuesday, September 15") listing that day's events with their time, or "All day". A day without events says "No events this day." A ✕ closes it; changing month clears the selection

change.title: Cap the chips
change.html:
"Sept 15 is a mess: three chips and the row is twice as tall as the others."

  • Show at most 2 chips per day.
  • If there are more, show a muted "+1 more" (the count of hidden events) under them. Sept 15 has 3 events.

hints: State: const [view, setView] = useState({ year: today.getFullYear(), month: today.getMonth() }); and use [view.year, view.month] as the effect dependencies.
Cells: const cells: (number | null)[] = []; push null firstWeekday(...) times, then 1..daysInMonth(...), then null while cells.length % 7 !== 0.
Month arithmetic: search mdn Date constructor month overflow. new Date(2026, 12, 1) is January 2027.
CSS: display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr));. The minmax(0, …) stops long chips from stretching a column.
Change: dayEvents.slice(0, 2) for the chips, and dayEvents.length - 2 for "+N more" when it is above 0.
Stretch: store selectedKey (the "YYYY-MM-DD" string), not a Date or the events. The panel's events are events.filter((e) => { return e.date === selectedKey; }).
rubric: Visible month in state, separate from today
Refetch effect keyed on year+month with cancelled guard
Cells derived (blanks + days + trailing blanks)
Year rollover handled by Date, not by hand
Reused date utils and EventChip
Grid uses CSS grid with minmax(0,1fr)
Chips capped with slice; hidden count derived

primitives.name: Month overflow in new Date
primitives.example:
new Date(2026, 12, 1)   // Jan 1 2027  (month 12 rolls into next year)
new Date(2026, -1, 1)   // Dec 1 2025
primitives.note: Months are 0-based (0 = January). Out-of-range months roll over, so read back getFullYear() / getMonth() instead of doing the math yourself.

primitives.name: Remainder %
primitives.note: Returns what is left over after dividing. while (cells.length % 7 !== 0) pads the last row.

primitives.name: Fixed column grid
primitives.example: .cal-grid { display: grid; grid-template-columns: repeat(7, minmax(0, 1fr)); gap: 6px; }
primitives.note: Seven equal columns. Plain 1fr has a min of "content size", so one long chip would widen its column; minmax(0, 1fr) doesn't.

primitives.name: First N items: slice
primitives.note: Returns a new array (end index not included) and never mutates. Safe when the array is shorter than n.

dc36.title: Chat: optimistic send
dc36.summary: A travel-concierge chat. Send messages optimistically with Sending… / Failed · Retry states, auto-scroll, and day separators.
dc36.brief:
The concierge chat of Wayfarer. ChatThread loads the conversation with getMessages() and renders MessageBubbles. The composer is a controlled input, but sending does nothing.

Read api.ts: sendMessage(text) takes 0.6–1.1s and returns the saved Message with a real id. To simulate a flaky network, a message containing "fail" throws the first time it's sent and succeeds on retry. utils/time.ts has formatTime, dayLabel and a fixed NOW_ISO.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change (~20 min): date separators.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–20 Core · 20–25 change · 25–30 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"Each message in state gets a status: sent, sending or failed. On submit I append a message with a temporary id and status sending, clear the input, and call the API. Success swaps the temp message for the server's one (matched by temp id); failure flips its status to failed. Retry sets it back to sending and calls the same deliver function. Auto-scroll is an effect on messages.length that sets scrollTop = scrollHeight on a ref to the scroll container."
requirements: Submitting the composer (Enter or Send) adds your message to the bottom immediately, faded, with "Sending…" under it, and clears the input. Empty or whitespace-only messages are ignored and Send is disabled while empty
When sendMessage resolves, the temporary message is replaced by the server's (real id) and shows its time ("3:01 PM")
If it throws, the bubble turns red and shows "Failed · Retry". Retry sets it back to "Sending…" and sends the same text again (it succeeds the second time)
The thread scrolls to the bottom after the first load and whenever a message is added

change.title: Date separators
change.html:
"It's hard to tell which day an answer came."

  • Before the first message of each day, show a centered pill separator with a line on both sides: Thu, Oct 8, Yesterday, Today (use dayLabel).
  • New messages sent today don't add another separator.

Hint: build the rows in a loop above the return, remembering the previous day label.

hints: Extend the type locally: type ChatMessage = Message & { status: "sent" | "sending" | "failed" }; and map the loaded messages to status: "sent".
Form submit: <form onSubmit={handleSubmit}> and e.preventDefault() first. Search: mdn preventDefault form submit.
Temp id: const tempId = "temp-" + Date.now(); Pass it to the API callback so you know which message to replace, even if two sends overlap.
Auto-scroll: useEffect(() => { const el = listRef.current; if (el) { el.scrollTop = el.scrollHeight; } }, [messages.length]); Search: mdn scrollHeight.

Change: build the rows above the return. const rows: React.ReactNode[] = []; let lastDay = ""; messages.forEach((m) => { const day = dayLabel(m.sentAt); if (day !== lastDay) { rows.push(...); lastDay = day; } rows.push(<MessageBubble ... />); });
rubric: Optimistic insert with a temp id
Success replaces by temp id; failure flips status (no mutation)
Retry reuses the same send function
Scroll handled with a ref + effect, not on every render
Form submit with preventDefault; empty blocked
Separators computed while building rows, using dayLabel

notes: max-w 75% · pad 9 12 · radius 16 (4 on the tail corner)

primitives.name: Extend a type with &
primitives.example: const m: ChatMessage = { id: 'temp-1', author: 'me', text: 'Hi', sentAt: NOW_ISO, status: 'sending' };
primitives.note: An intersection: every field of Message plus status. Keeps UI-only fields out of the API type.

primitives.name: Form submit without reload
primitives.note: A <button type="submit"> and pressing Enter in the input both fire onSubmit; without preventDefault the page reloads.

primitives.name: Temporary id: Date.now()
primitives.note: Date.now() returns milliseconds since 1970 as a number. Good enough for a short-lived client id you swap for the server's.

primitives.name: Append immutably
primitives.note: Spread copies the old items into a new array. push would mutate state and React may not re-render.

primitives.name: Build a list with forEach + "previous" variable
primitives.syntax:
let last = '';
arr.forEach((x) => { if (x.day !== last) { rows.push(sep); last = x.day; } rows.push(row); });
primitives.example: let last = ''; ['Thu', 'Thu', 'Today'].forEach((d) => { if (d !== last) { console.log('sep', d); last = d; } });   // sep Thu, sep Today
primitives.note: forEach returns undefined; you collect into your own array. Use it when one input item can produce 0, 1 or 2 output rows.

dc37.title: City autocomplete
dc37.summary: A flight search "To" field. Suggestions from an API as you type, click to pick, keyboard support, then match highlighting.
dc37.brief:
The search hero of skyhop. SearchPanel renders a CityInput for "To", which is just a controlled input right now.

Read api.ts: searchCities(query) takes 0.25–0.7s, so responses can arrive out of order while typing. getRecentSearches() takes 0.2–0.5s. utils/format.ts has formatCity ("Lisbon, Portugal").

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change (~26 min): highlight the match.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–26 Core · 26–31 change · 31–40 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"All state lives in CityInput: query, results, loading, open. An effect on query calls the API with a cancelled flag, which also fixes out-of-order responses. Selecting fills the input with formatCity and closes. Closing on blur would kill the click on an option, so options use onMouseDown + preventDefault. For the keyboard I add one activeIndex that both arrows and hover change; Enter picks results[activeIndex]."

primitives.name: Ignore stale responses (effect cleanup)
primitives.syntax: useEffect(() => { let cancelled = false; api(q).then((d) => { if (!cancelled) { set(d); } }); return () => { cancelled = true; }; }, [q]);
primitives.example: // type 'l' then 'lo': the 'l' effect's cleanup runs first, so its late response is dropped

primitives.name: Keep focus while clicking: mousedown + preventDefault
primitives.note: Event order is mousedown → blur → mouseup → click. Preventing mousedown's default stops the input from losing focus, so your onBlur doesn't close the list first.

primitives.name: Find a substring: indexOf
primitives.note: Returns the index of the first match, or -1. Lowercase both sides for a case-insensitive search, but slice the original text so the casing is kept.

primitives.name: Cut a string: slice(start, end)
primitives.note: End index is not included; omit it to go to the end. Three slices give before / match / after.

dc38.title: File explorer tree
dc38.summary: An in-browser IDE. Build a recursive, expandable file tree, open files in the preview, then add folder file counts.
dc38.brief:
The editor of Codebox, a dark IDE. Explorer loads the nested tree with getTree() but only lists the top level; folders don't open. Preview is already done: give it a fileId and it loads the file with getFile (0.3–0.8s, stale-safe) and shows it in CodeView. Right now it always gets null.

Read api.ts (folders have children) and components/TreeRow.tsx: one styled row that takes depth (indent), isOpen (chevron), isSelected and an extra slot on the right. It does not render children: that's your job. utils/files.ts has fileIcon and formatBytes.

Pass bar: Core 1–2 working. Strong: plus 3–4. Change (~27 min): folder file counts.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–6 plan out loud · 6–27 Core · 27–32 change · 32–40 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"A TreeNode component renders one TreeRow and, if it's an open folder, maps its children to TreeNode again with depth + 1. Expanded folders are one Set of ids in Explorer, not state in each node, so they survive re-renders and can be cleared at once. The selected file is needed by both the explorer (highlight) and the preview (load), so it lives in App. Each node can pass its path down, so on select I already have the breadcrumb."
requirements: Folders toggle open/closed on click (TreeRow rotates the chevron when isOpen). Children are indented one level deeper (depth + 1), to any depth (src/utils/api/client.ts is 3 levels deep). src starts open

Clicking a file highlights it (isSelected) and the Preview loads it ("Loading…" then the code). Clicking another file quickly never shows the first file's content. Collapsing a folder that contains the selected file keeps it selected and previewed
The preview header shows a breadcrumb: codebox-web › src › components › Button.tsx (last part bold), with the size still on the right
A Collapse all button in the Explorer header closes every folder (disabled when nothing is open)
The tree has role="tree"; each item is role="treeitem" and folders have aria-expanded

change.title: Folder file counts
change.html:
"Tell me how big folders are before I open them."

  • Each folder shows a small muted pill on the right with the number of files inside it, counting all nested folders (src shows 9, components shows 3).
  • Files show no pill. Pass it through TreeRow's extra prop.

Hint: the count is recursive too, as a plain function.

hints: Recursive component: function TreeNode({ node, depth, ... }) { ... children = node.children.map((child) => { return <TreeNode key={child.id} node={child} depth={depth + 1} ... />; }) }. Search: react recursive component tree.
Set in state: never .add on the current set. setExpanded((prev) => { const next = new Set(prev); if (next.has(id)) { next.delete(id); } else { next.add(id); } return next; }). Search: mdn Set.
Lift the selection: App holds selectedId, passes it to Explorer (for isSelected) and <Preview fileId={selectedId} />.
Breadcrumb: pass parentPath down. Each node computes const path = [...parentPath, node.name]; and sends it up with onSelect({ id, path }).
Change: function countFiles(node: FileNode): number { if (node.type === "file") { return 1; } let total = 0; (node.children || []).forEach((c) => { total = total + countFiles(c); }); return total; }
rubric: Recursive TreeNode passing depth + 1
Expanded state as one immutable Set at the top
Selection lifted to App (explorer + preview both need it)
Reused TreeRow, Preview, CodeView, formatBytes
Path built while recursing, not searched afterwards
Recursive count as a pure function
Collapse all is a single setExpanded(new Set())

primitives.name: Recursive component
primitives.syntax: function TreeNode({ node, depth }) { ... node.children.map((c) => { return <TreeNode key={c.id} node={c} depth={depth + 1} />; }) }
primitives.note: A component may render itself. The recursion stops naturally at files and at closed folders (nothing to map).

primitives.name: Set in state: copy, then add/delete
primitives.syntax: const next = new Set(prev); next.add(id); return next;
primitives.note: .add/.delete mutate the Set. Copy with new Set(prev) first, or React sees the same object and skips the re-render.

primitives.name: Default for a missing array: || []
primitives.note: Files have no children; || [] gives an empty array so .map/.forEach don't crash.

primitives.name: Recursive function
primitives.syntax: function count(n) { if (leaf) { return 1; } let t = 0; n.children.forEach((c) => { t = t + count(c); }); return t; }
primitives.example: countFiles({ type: 'folder', children: [{ type: 'file' }, { type: 'folder', children: [{ type: 'file' }] }] })   // 2
primitives.note: Every recursive function needs a base case (a file returns 1) and a step that calls itself on smaller pieces.

dc39.title: Employee directory table
dc39.summary: An HR directory. Combine search, a department filter and sortable columns, then paginate and handle the empty state.
dc39.brief:
The Directory page of Peoplebase. EmployeeTable loads all 28 employees with getEmployees() (0.5–1.1s) and renders every one. The columns are already driven by one COLUMNS config: the header maps over it, and EmployeeRow renders the cells with renderCell.

Read components/: Pagination (Prev / "Page 2 of 4" / Next) and DeptBadge already exist. DEPARTMENTS is exported from api.ts. The stylesheet already has .toolbar, .search, .select, .btn, .btn-link, .table-foot and .range.

Timeline: 0–3 read · 3–7 plan out loud · 7–27 Core · 27–33 change · 33–40 Next and talk.

Reference "plan out loud" (open after saying yours)

"The only state is the inputs: query, dept, sortKey, sortDir, later page. Everything else is a pipeline computed on each render: filter by query, filter by department, copy and sort, then slice the page. Every handler that changes a filter also sets page back to 1, because page 3 of the old list might not exist. The header is already a map over COLUMNS, so each <th> just becomes a sort button."

primitives.name: Sort a copy
primitives.note: sort() mutates the array in place (and returns it). Copy first so you never reorder state. The callback returns negative / 0 / positive.

primitives.name: Compare strings: localeCompare
primitives.note: Returns -1, 0 or 1, exactly what sort wants. For descending, return -result.

primitives.name: Controlled <select>

primitives.name: Caret position: selectionStart
primitives.note: Returns the index of the caret in the text (a number). Read it in onChange to look only at what was typed before the caret.

primitives.name: RegExp.exec() with groups
primitives.note: Returns null or an array: [0] is the whole match, [1], [2]… the parenthesised groups. $ anchors to the end (the caret).

primitives.name: Replace a range: slice + concat
primitives.example:
const t = 'Hi @pa ok';
t.slice(0, 3) + '@Paula Reyes ' + t.slice(6)   // 'Hi @Paula Reyes  ok'
primitives.note: Strings are immutable: build a new string from the part before and the part after.

primitives.name: Put the caret back: setSelectionRange
primitives.note: Same start and end = a caret, no selection. Run it after React has written the new value (next frame), or React moves the caret again.

primitives.name: useRef to reach a DOM node
primitives.example: const el = ref.current;   // the <textarea>, or null before mount
primitives.note: ref.current is the DOM element. Changing a ref does not re-render. Check for null before using it.
